title: The 25 Best Left Backs in World Soccer—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffJul 14, 2025Nuno Mendes has fulfilled his early career potential.  / Franco Arland/Getty ImagesFor years, the left back position was overlooked, often seen as a defensive afterthought rather than a key role.

But the modern game has completely flipped that script. Thanks to tactical innovators like Pep Guardiola and others, the left back role has become one of the most challenging and influential positions on the field. Today’s left backs are expected to do it all: defend with discipline, cover endless ground and contribute creatively to the attack.
This evolution has produced a new breed of left back—versatile, dynamic and often among the standout players on their teams.
Here’s Sports Illustrated’s look at the current best in the business.

Andy Robertson joined Spurs in the summer. / Steve Christo/Corbis/Getty Images.Andy Robertson may now be past his blistering peak—the form that once had many calling him the best left back in the world—but make no mistake: he still has plenty to offer.Sure, the explosive pace that once defined his overlapping runs may have dipped slightly, dulling some of his impact in the final third. Yet the Scotsman remains a tenacious defender—solid in every challenge, relentless in recovery and never giving an opponent a moment’s peace.He’s also an unapologetically vocal leader. Make a mistake near him? You’ll hear about it immediately—and probably get a detailed rundown on how to fix it next time.That, perhaps, is why Tottenham Hotspur decided to acquire him after several difficult seasons.

Ian Maatsen. / Rene Nijhuis/MB Media/Getty ImagesOne of many former Chelsea full backs on this list, Ian Maatsen is growing in importance for Aston Villa, particularly following Lucas Digne’s return to PSG.An electric force going forward, Maatsen excels at progressive ball-carrying and high-tempo build-up play, giving both Villa and the Netherlands, when given the chance, plenty of energy in the final third.He’s also more than happy to drift inside and operate as an inverted full back—or even a midfielder—to get more involved in the build-up. That versatility makes him a fascinating tactical weapon, capable of creating overloads in midfield before bursting forward into the space in front of him.He may not be the most imposing defender on this list, but his recovery pace is fierce. Even when he gets caught high up the pitch, Maatsen has the speed to make up ground in a hurry and get himself back into the defensive picture.

Wesley is increasingly influential for club and country. / Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesOriginally schooled as a right back, Wesley has been increasingly deployed on his unnatural flank by Gian Piero Gasperini during Roma’s flexible evolution under the cerebral Italian.“He’s a growing player,” Gasperini beamed last year. “Very strong.”The tenacious and versatile Brazilian was unfortunate to miss the 2026 World Cup through injury, thus missing an opportunity to showcase his talents to an even wider audience. But his performances for Roma, which involve him scuttling up and down the field as a flying wing back, surely won’t go under the radar for much longer.

Maxi Araújo has been superb for Sporting. / Torbjorn Tande/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesAt the 2026 World Cup against Cape Verde, Maxi Araújo became the first Uruguayan player in 56 years to register both a goal and an assist in the same World Cup match. The last to achieve the feat was Juan Martín Mujica in 1970.Araújo also found the net in Uruguay’s tournament opener against Saudi Arabia, underlining just how much of an attacking threat he can be from the left flank. Those qualities have been on full display for Sporting CP too, with the versatile full back thriving since his move from Mexico in 2024.Explosive, direct and always looking to make something happen in the final third, Araújo has quickly established himself as one of the most exciting attacking players in his position.It feels like only a matter of time before one of Europe’s giants comes calling.

Lucas Digne has returned to Paris. / Aurélien Meunier/PSG/Getty Images.There are certainly bumps to Lucas Digne’s game. The left back can make rash and costly decisions, but those odd lapses in concentration don’t overshadow the quality he provides. Wicked deliveries into the penalty area are a staple of his game, with that excellent distribution often showcased at corners and free kicks for France and, previously, Aston Villa.  Digne’s entering the twilight of his career and continues to divide opinion somewhat, but there’s a reason he’s represented Lille, PSG, Roma, Barcelona, Everton and Villa over the years.

Myles Lewis-Skelly is a smooth operator. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesMyles Lewis-Skelly plays—and carries himself—with the kind of swagger that some find off-putting. But like Jude Bellingham, it’s that very self-belief that allows him to perform at such a high level despite his age. Call it arrogance if you want, but when you’ve got the talent to back it up, who’s really complaining?And Lewis-Skelly does have the talent. He’s a fierce competitor, relentless in and out of possession and refuses to let any cause die. But he’s not just grit and drive—technically, he’s elite. He can glide past players with ease, pick out teammates with precision and break lines with his dribbling and passing. That combination of tenacity and technical brilliance is exactly why he’s been trusted in midfield roles (that arguably suit him better) despite his youth.

Andrea Cambiaso is an underappreciated talent. / Francesco Scaccianoce/Getty ImagesVersatile wingback Andrea Cambiaso has been like a Swiss Army knife for Juventus since breaking into the first team in 2023–24, able to fill multiple roles with ease. Over the past two seasons, he’s been used not only as a traditional full back, but also in an inverted role and further forward on the wing, showing his tactical flexibility.Cambiaso is a do-it-all performer: solid defensively, dynamic going forward and comfortable adapting to multiple positions. His versatility, combined with relentless work rate, has made him indispensable during a period of transition at the club, as Juventus have navigated squad changes and sought to redefine their identity.He may rarely grab the headlines with flashy moments, but Cambiaso’s consistent impact on the pitch makes him one of the most valuable and reliable players in the Juventus squad.

Maximilian Mittelstädt has thrived at Stuttgart. / Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesMaximilian Mittelstädt is a late bloomer in comparison to many of his positional peers, but the left back’s switch to Stuttgart in 2023 helped propel him toward his potential. Flourishing in Sebastian Hoeneß’s high-octane, Mittelstädt has been super consistent for one of the Bundesliga’s resurgent forces, particularly catching the eye with his explosive displays in the final third. Each campaign with VfB has yielded more goal involvements than the last, with seven followed by 11 and then, in 2025–26, an impressive 13. Such stellar showings have earned him plenty of appearances for Germany, too.

Rayan Aït-Nouri has stagnated at Man City. / Molly Darlington/Getty ImagesRayan Aït-Nouri is a serious baller.The Algerian dazzles with silky feet that could easily be mistaken for those of more attack-minded countrymen like Riyad Mahrez and Saïd Benrahma. He can turn on a dime, glide past defenders with jaw-dropping ease and make dribbling look effortless.But Aït-Nouri isn’t simply a flashy winger trapped in a fullback’s body—he pairs that flair with the vision and creativity of a top-tier playmaker, making him a constant threat whenever he gets forward.Defensively, there’s still room for improvement, which perhaps explains why he has struggled for minutes at Manchester City behind Nico O’Reilly, whom we’ll get to later. Still, Aït-Nouri remains a stellar player, even if his future may ultimately lie elsewhere.

Milos Kerkez has had a tough start to life at Liverpool. / Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesMilos Kerkez hasn’t quite lived up to the lofty expectations he set at Bournemouth since his 2025 move to Liverpool.Part of that, however, can be attributed to the chaos surrounding him at Anfield. Managerial changes and an evolving squad have hardly provided the ideal environment for a young player to settle, and with plenty of time still on his side, Kerkez has every opportunity to prove the doubters wrong.Because there’s no doubting the talent. Explosively quick, physically imposing and armed with a delivery that could make David Beckham do a double take, Kerkez has all the ingredients of a modern full back. Now, it’s simply about finding that level consistently for the Reds.

Adrien Truffert has quickly impressed in England. /  Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesWhen it became apparent that Milos Kerkez’s stint at Bournemouth would be relatively short and sweet, thoughts quickly turned to who could replace the impressive Hungarian. It didn’t take long for the Cherries to settle on Rennes captain Adrien Truffert.It didn’t take Truffert long to show exactly why he had been one of Ligue 1’s standout performers, either. The Frenchman is not only highly capable in one-vs-one situations defensively, but also a tremendous attacking threat who loves to whip the ball into the penalty area.Throw in his dynamism and athleticism, which see him charge up and down the pitch with a seemingly never-ending battery life, and Bournemouth don’t miss Kerkez at all.

Alejandro Balde has fallen down the pecking order in Catalonia. / David Ramirez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesIt once looked like Barcelona had found the perfect heir to Jordi Alba’s throne in Alejandro Balde.That hasn’t quite been how things have transpired so far, but the potential is still there.Balde broke out in style during the 2022–23 season as Xavi’s side stormed to the La Liga title. The following year proved more difficult, however, with injuries and inconsistency halting his momentum and eventually forcing him to the sidelines.Since then, though, Balde has bounced back. Fully fit and firing, he has re-established himself as one of Barça’s most important players, playing a key role in their back-to-back La Liga triumphs in 2024–25 and 2025–26. His trademark bursts down the flank, improved decision-making and ever-growing defensive maturity have made him a constant asset at both ends of the pitch.

David Raum is so consistent. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesLike many modern left backs, David Raum excels with his head down, bursting toward the opposition goal. That attacking threat has made him one of Germany’s most impactful defenders over recent years. RB Leipzig have benefitted from his fierce speed, relentless running and turbo-charged left boot. He delivered 12 goal involvements for the Bundesliga outfit in 2025–26, which was his second-best return since joining the club. Defensively, Raum is very solid, too. The physicality which makes him deadly in the opponent’s half also helps snuff out danger and thwart a band of tricky right wingers in Germany and beyond.

Álvaro Carreras joined Real Madrid in 2025. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesManchester United have long been desperate for a reliable left back. Yet somehow, they let one of the brightest young talents slip right through their fingers: Álvaro Carreras.Signed by United in 2022, he was quietly sold to Benfica just a couple of years later for a bargain price after a few loan spells. Carreras quickly blossomed into one of Portugal’s hottest young prospects—and arguably its best left back—so it was perhaps no surprise when Real Madrid paid the big bucks to take him home to Spain.Carreras has that rare blend of sharp tactical awareness, blistering pace and flair that turns defence into attack. His progressive passing and fearless runs down the flank have made him a standout performer for Los Blancos.
